The Retirement age in Trinidad and Tobago - National Insurance Board of Trinidad and Tobago

_: Public-sector retirement ages vary: 60 for most employees, 62 for Indian Railways, service chiefs and for high court judges; 65 for Supreme Court judges and the Chief of Defence Staff. In the private sector, retirement age depends on the company, up to a maximum of 65.

In the U.S., retirement age depends on birth year. You can retire as early as 62, but benefits are reduced by about 25–30%. Full benefits start at 66 for those born before 1960 and 67 for those born after. Delaying benefits until 70 increases the monthly amount.
Retirement age increases by one year every three years until it reaches 65 in 2043.
